stops.name: The Haunebu discs, the great craft
stops.campa: Alongside the Vril line rise the Haunebu, the heavy discs. The Haunebu I, twenty-five metres across, carries eight; the Haunebu II grows to thirty and more; and by the war's last winter the drawings promise a Haunebu III of seventy-one metres, a ship built not to patrol but to cross the void. These are the machines the wartime legend hangs its whole faith upon: that beneath the collapsing Reich a fleet of the beyond was being forged in secret works, tuned to a star.

stops.name: Kolberg, the Vril gathering and the Aldebaran Project
stops.campa: In December 1943 Maria and the medium Sigrun come to Kolberg on the Baltic, where the circle meets to weigh the boldest of all its plans: the Aldebaran Project, not to fly the Earth but to leave it, to send a crewed disc across the sixty-eight light-years to the world that first spoke to Maria's hand. The women who began with braids and a moving pencil now sit at the planning of an interstellar voyage. The star that called them, they resolve, will be answered in the flesh.

stops.name: Berlin: Hitler, Himmler, and the plan for Vril-7
stops.campa: On the twenty-second of January 1944 the highest of the Reich sit with the circle: Hitler, Himmler, Professor Schumann, and the Vril man Kunkel bend over the design of the Vril-7 and the question of a dimension-channel: a fold in space through which the disc might reach Aldebaran without crossing the light-years one by one. The séance of a Croatian girl has climbed, in the mythos, to the war council of a continent. What began as a voice in Munich is now a matter of state strategy.

stops.name: Hamilton, Ohio: Symmes and the world within
stops.campa: The mythos of the bases has an older father across the sea. In 1818 an American soldier, John Cleves Symmes, sends out his Circular No. 1 and declares the earth hollow and habitable within, holding solid spheres one inside the other and open at the poles some twelve or sixteen degrees. He begs a hundred brave men to sail past the eighty-second parallel to a warm land stocked with beasts and perhaps men. No ship goes; but the idea of the peopled inside and the polar door is loosed, and a century on it will shelter the discs beneath the ice and the beings the circle says await them.
stops.quote: I declare the earth is hollow, and habitable within; containing a number of solid concentric spheres, one within the other, and that it is open at the poles 12 or 16 degrees.
stops.quote_source: John Cleves Symmes Jr., 'Circular No. 1', 10 April 1818

stops.name: The Vril-7 through the dimension-channel, the aged ship returns
stops.campa: As the year turns the circle attempts what it planned. The Vril-7 is sent through the dimension-channel toward Aldebaran, and when it comes back it comes back wrong: the tradition says the craft returned as though aged, its surfaces weathered and damaged, as if it had spent in an instant a longer time than it left. The channel is real, the mythos concludes, and it is terrible; the fold in space exacts a toll. Yet the road to the star is shown open, and the vanishing is now conceivable.

stops.name: Munich / Berlin, the last letter, 'niemand bleibt hier'
stops.campa: On the eleventh of March 1945, as the Reich burns down around them, the last document of the Vril Gesellschaft passes among the circle in Maria's hand. It says almost nothing and it says everything: none of us stays. Then the medium of Zagreb, the woman of striking beauty who heard Aldebaran in her fingers, steps out of every record that ever held her. No death, no grave, no body, no further word: only the three German words and the silence after them. The circle says she went to the star. History says only that she is gone.
stops.quote_source: The final Vril Gesellschaft letter attributed to Maria Orsic, 11 March 1945 (as reported in the postwar tradition)

stops.name: Neuschwabenland, the Antarctic redoubt, Base 211
stops.campa: Six weeks after the last letter, far south on the ice the Reich's expedition named Neuschwabenland, the legend raises Base 211: a hollow beneath the world where the discs are said to shelter as the Reich falls. From here, the boldest tellings hold, a great Haunebu lifts on the twenty-first of April 1945 and is gone, bound not for any earthly port but outward. So the vanishing is answered in machinery: the bases below the ice and the beings within the earth close the circle Symmes once opened, the hollow world and the hollow pole, and the ships that pass between the star and the snow.

stops.name: Lyon, Savitri Devi and the avatar of the age
stops.campa: In the postwar penumbra a Frenchwoman born Maximiani Portas, calling herself Savitri Devi, gives the defeated cause a religion. In 'The Lightning and the Sun' she names Hitler an avatar come down to fight the dark tide of the Kali Yuga, the age of dissolution. She has no discs and no séance, but she supplies the myth its scripture of cosmic time and Hyperborean descent: the frame in which a star-born Aryan people, a vanished medium, and a fleet gone to Aldebaran can all be read as one sacred story continuing beyond its worldly ruin.

stops.name: Paris, the legend printed, 'Le Matin des magiciens'
stops.campa: Fifteen years after the vanishing, in Paris, Louis Pauwels and Jacques Bergier open the door of the legend to the world. In 'Le Matin des magiciens' they tell of a Vril Society, an inner circle of the Thule, occultists in old Berlin who sought pacts with hidden powers. They give no proof and, at first, no Maria; but the tale takes fire, and out of it grow the later tellings that will name her, braid her hair, and send her disc to Aldebaran. Here the mythos she is said to have lived first becomes a book that others can read.

stops.name: Santiago de Chile, Serrano and the flight to the stars
stops.campa: In Chile the diplomat and poet Miguel Serrano crowns the tradition. His esoteric Hitlerism tells of Hyperborean Aryans of extraterrestrial origin, image-bearers of the godhead, warred upon by an evil Demiurge; of the hollow earth and hidden Shambhala; of leaders and craft that did not die but withdrew: to the poles, to the inner world, to the stars. In his cosmos Maria Orsic's disc and her three last words find their final meaning: not a disappearance but a departure, the light-god people going home the way they came, answering at last the star that first moved a girl's hand in Zagreb.
